about: Paper 2's provenance ledger: how the model was built, stage by stage, and what each stage changed. Hand-kept. A stage enters when it changed a stated result, when it was a check that could have failed, or when it replaced a convention; bugs fixed on the way stay in the code history and four/CLAUDE.md. 'before' values are historical (they are no longer in the data) and name where they were recorded; every 'now' with a check is recomputed from the committed data by build.mjs, which stops if they disagree. 'rule' is the decision rule fixed before the stage's results came in, or null when none was, which the supplement then says.

stages.title: What the first generation gives back
stages.replaced: returns judged on zero-age stars (nuclei.mjs giveback, starmix, cores: declared lifetimes, stirred cores at zero age)
stages.by: the aged mass ladders at G 1e-17 (six strengths, 0.25–4 M_Ch): each star's processed core at its run's end and its return under declared endings (core growth g 1/1.25/1.5; dead remnants returning their envelope and w 3%/30% of the core's ash; explosion at the Chandrasekhar mass with nuclei.mjs explode's burn shares, expansion f 30/100), then the net yield p on a mass function (alpha 2.35/1.9, 0.25–2.5 M_Ch at every strength, stars dying within 10/30 Gyr) and one-zone galaxies (fusion/tools/yields4.mjs). A first pass on the s 1.5152 ladder alone (p 0.027–0.14) was superseded before it was committed; two slips found on the way: ladders starting at the analogue mass left out the low-mass stars that lock mass away (p above 1 at s 1.55), and the galaxy gave a star born with metals its full primordial ash on top of them (gas Z above 1)

moved.before: none computed on aged stars (zero-age giveback: declared lifetimes)
moved.after: mostly the rock row from exploding cores; much smaller from s 1.7 up. evolve4-11 to -13 carried all 12 cut stars to the end (28 of 29 short-lived stars reached Xc 10⁻³; s 1.65 4 M_Ch stops at Xc 0.0033), and the last stretch mattered: ash grew by up to a quarter (s 1.55, 2.5 M_Ch: 33% to 41% of the star) and turned heavier (elements 12–15 leading), which raised p's band at s ≤ 1.55 from 0.042–0.17 (evolve4-10; 0.048–0.23 after evolve4-11) and, at s 1.55, iron's share of p from 1% to 19%. An exploding core's ash is now burnt element by element on explode's rows, weighted by mass (it had taken the leading element's row for all of it, so the split jumped when the lead flipped). The last star in (s 1.5152, 1.25 M_Ch) grew a core just over the Chandrasekhar mass at g 1.25, so it explodes at the middle choice too, and a core only just at the limit burns mostly to iron: at s 1.5152 the middle choice returns iron and the rock row about equally (p 0.095 → 0.15), and over the choices iron is 15–63% of p at s ≤ 1.55. stages.title: Where an exploding core's ash goes
stages.replaced: an exploding core's burn shares taken from nuclei.mjs explode's row nearest the core's paper mass (rows up to 1.1 M_Ch: cores that cannot stand above the limit, contracting hot to ignition at lower density), and the share burnt to equilibrium placed on the Minnesota drop's single most bound nucleus (element 137, mass 274); the iron near our strength came out 23% / 47% / 24% of p at g 1 / 1.25 / 1.5, not monotonic, and the rock row most of the rest
stages.by: every exploding core burnt as explode's core at the limit (its 0.9999 row): a 4D core reaches its ash's ignition temperature only within 4 × 10⁻⁴ of the Chandrasekhar mass, at ~7 × 10²⁷ kg/m⁴ (electron Fermi momentum ~50 m_e c, ours ~10), so it burns 97–100% to equilibrium at explode's f 30–100 (calibrated on ours); the rock row takes over only at f ~10⁴–10⁵ (scan, 2026-11-24). Equilibrium spread by fusion/tools/nse4.mjs: 4D nuclear statistical equilibrium on the trusted MN s 1.5152 b 1.4 drop (Y_e 0.5, ground states, helium-4 at its computed binding) at that density over f and a declared freeze-out 5–10 GK, then β-decay at fixed mass to the most bound charge (m_n − m_H ours, declared); no alpha decay, fission or proton emission open on the masses that carry it. The same at-the-limit row in nuclei.mjs cores (the book's chapter 15 table). yields4.mjs on the same inputs reproduced the published yields4.json byte for byte before the change.
